column3: Everything below is now on the preview link at sunny-home-services.vercel.app. All 114 pages were loaded from it and checked; every one answers. The pages are also served at addresses without a .html ending, so /millcreek-ut reaches the Millcreek page, matching the addresses listed in this log.
sunny-home-theme.css and sunny-v2.css were in the css folder but no page loaded either one. Removed, so what ships is only what runs.

No heading, paragraph, list item or button now leaves a single word alone on its last line, at any width from 360 to 1440. The last two words of 6,532 text blocks are tied together so they wrap as a pair, and a final word containing a hyphen is held whole. Nothing was reworded: comparing the visible text of every page before and after shows no word changed.

Seventy five service grids across fifty pages were still the old cards, squeezed inside the narrow heading rail and running down the page. They are tiles now, across the full column, and every set lands in at most two rows with nothing stranded on the last one. Drain cleaning came down from 1,836px to 962px. Six grids of photographs were lifted out of the rail as well; they keep their pictures.

A card with a photograph and a tile without one now behave identically on hover: the same lift, shadow, blue border and gold bar across the top. They had been lifting by different amounts, and only the tile had the bar.

All 30 technician photographs were checked against the rule that the Sunny logo appears on the hat, on the chest and across the back. Twenty five already did. Five did not, all in the same set, and they carried a plain cap and polo or a mark that was not Sunny's. Those five were remade with the real logo referenced, and they appear on 33 pages between them.

Sections no longer fade in on scroll. Everything is drawn with the page. A side effect worth having: the stylesheet started those elements at zero opacity so the script could animate them in, which meant a visitor with JavaScript blocked saw an almost empty page. Now the page reads either way. The markup keeps its classes so the animation can be switched back on.

The three ductless service cards sat two-up inside the heading rail and spilled onto a second row. They run three across the full column now, and the section came down from 1,506px to 893px. The photographs were kept.

The furnace repair and mini-split pages now show manufacturer logos where a correct one could be sourced: Carrier, Lennox, Rheem and Goodman on one, Mitsubishi Electric and Daikin on the other. The remaining brands stay as names on an "and more" line. Sources and licensing are in assets/brands/SOURCES.md.

Tiles, ticked cards and numbered steps now respond to the pointer: a lift, a shadow, a gold bar across the top of a tile, and the Learn More sliding with it. The reveal animation leaves an inline transform on everything it touches, which had been silently cancelling the lift on the original cards across the whole site; that is fixed too. Anyone who has asked their system for less movement gets the color change without the motion.

The two card grids that carry information rather than links, on the water heater repair and furnace repair pages, now match the service tiles and run across the full column instead of inside the narrow heading rail.
Every band on a service or city page now carries a washed texture. The alternating tone bands were a flat fill with their texture switched off, and 22 bands across 21 pages had no texture at all.

Ticked items read as cards with a gold edge rather than loose lines, so a short item no longer sits beside empty space. Numbered steps run across in one row. On the Salt Lake City plumbing page the service list became linked tiles, so each service reaches its own page; it was prose with no way through. That page lost 600px.

The body font mapped every weight onto one medium file, so bold text rendered no differently from the text around it. The 700 weight was already in assets/fonts and unused; it is now wired to weights 600 and above.

The West Jordan plumbing page moved from eight photo cards to the same tiles the city pages use, run across the full column so every service title fits one line. Its eight mismatched illustrations came out; the twelve links inside that copy were kept. That section went from 2,046px to 791px.

A ticked list inside a heading rail ran as one tall column, so a short item held a whole line and left the rest empty. Two columns now, with a lone last item taking the full width. The sub-headings that follow a list no longer sit straight on top of it, and the line that introduces a list reads as a lead-in rather than body copy.

Removed the three remaining plumbing illustrations that used a stand-in sun with the wrong cap. Nothing references them now. The corrected fixtures illustration stays in assets/services/ and is not in use.

Replaced the photo service cards on the city pages with compact tiles. A photo per service made those sections three screens tall and forced the same artwork onto unrelated services. Each set now lands in two rows.

Redrew the plumbing fixtures card. The earlier one had a stand-in sun character with the wrong cap rather than the brand mascot. The gas line, garbage disposal and toilet cards on the plumbing page still have the same problem and are waiting on a decision.

Turned 136 straight apostrophes into curly ones across 22 pages, which had been mixed with 1,630 curly ones, and closed three stray spaces before a comma or a period. No wording changed. The four mirrored pages were left untouched so they still match the live site.

Built four service-area pages from the approved briefs: the Millcreek hub, Millcreek heating, Millcreek plumbers and the Kearns hub. Both cities added to the grids on the home page and the service area page.

Raised every tap target to 44px across all pages: menu button, header and footer links, breadcrumbs, service area chips, buttons, ZIP titles, form submits and card links. Fixed a checklist tick that sat level with the middle of a wrapped line instead of its first line.

Rolled the Kliemann-style layout across the service pages: a sticky heading rail beside the text, alternating tinted bands, and full-bleed photo splits, so a page no longer reads as one centered column all the way down.
Corrected three pages whose developer comment still carried Lehi's production URL. Gave a lone trailing service card the full row.
Built the blog: an index, 13 articles from their briefs, and an annotated template for dev to duplicate. Restructured the article layout into two-column chapters after review.

Added license number 14291812-5501 and Instagram and Facebook links to the footer of every page. Evened out the service card icons and turned the bulleted copy back into paragraphs on the two pages named.
Built Salt Lake City AC, heating and plumber, plus the whole-house air purifier page, from the supplied briefs.

Put West Jordan back where the briefs had it. The live site had the city swapped for the region by a find and replace, which left titles reading "Wasatch Front, UT", a "Wasatch Front Building and Safety Division" that does not exist, and one city's elevation applied to a 120-mile region. Not yet confirmed by the client.
